stories.title: White blood cell DNA may strengthen cancer signals
stories.summary: A four-year study of 1,480 participants across 43 Indian hospitals found that higher levels of circulating DNA in cancer patients improved detection sensitivity. The research, published in PNAS, challenges the long-held assumption that DNA released by white blood cells dilutes cancer signals in blood-based tests.

stories.title: Hyderabad doctor lowers rare disease drug cost
stories.summary: Seven children with Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome will receive a year of tiratricol for free on November 30. The initiative, led by paediatrician Dr. Sivaranjani Santosh and Access to Medicines India, reduced the annual treatment cost from 9 crore rupees to 2.5 lakh rupees per patient.

stories.title: Early rituximab use eases gMG symptoms
stories.summary: A real-world study shows that treating adults with generalized myasthenia gravis with rituximab within two years of diagnosis eases symptoms and reduces corticosteroid use. The benefits were also observed in patients with late-disease onset and those with conditions that are typically hard to treat.

stories.title: Inhaled IPF treatment trial reports early data
stories.summary: Rein Therapeutics reports that one-third of participants in a Phase 2 trial for an inhaled idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis treatment showed improved lung function after 12 weeks. Researchers do not yet know which participants received the experimental drug LTI-03 and which received a placebo.

stories.title: Blood test may identify lymphoma immunotherapy response
stories.summary: Cornell and Dana-Farber researchers found that RNA floating in plasma carries a signature of a lymphoma tumor's surroundings. This signature tracked with whether patients remained in remission one year after treatment, potentially helping to identify who will respond to immunotherapy.

stories.title: Brain changes in pregnancy may offer MS insights
stories.summary: Researchers at The Alfred and Monash University are studying decreased brain volume in pregnant women with multiple sclerosis. While doctors previously worried these changes indicated disease progression, the team is now investigating whether this biological process could lead to a cure.

stories.title: Compound shows promise for nerve repair in MS
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and Japanese collaborators report that a derivative of a natural compound reduced multiple sclerosis symptoms in a mouse model. The study suggests the compound may promote regenerative pathways within the central nervous system.

stories.title: Dual-targeted CAR T-cell therapy shows promise in patients with treatment-resistant multiple myeloma - Medical Xpress
AIIMS performs first fetal spine surgery
stories.summary: A team at AIIMS Delhi performed India's first open fetal surgery on November 12, repairing a spinal defect in a 25-week-old fetus. The six-hour procedure required surgeons to open the uterus and lift the baby's back through a 6 to 8 cm window.

stories.title: AIIMS completes milestone fetal surgery
stories.summary: Doctors at AIIMS Delhi successfully repaired a myelomeningocele spinal defect in a 25-week-old fetus during a six-hour procedure on November 12. The surgery marks a new capability in Indian fetal medicine, with both the mother and the baby reported to be recovering well.

stories.title: AIIMS details challenges of fetal surgery
stories.summary: Doctors at AIIMS Delhi described the six-hour procedure to repair a fetal spinal defect as a significant challenge. The team focused on safely opening and closing the uterus while ensuring the fetus remained correctly positioned for the duration of the surgery.

stories.title: Health Ministry seeks tighter antimicrobial rules
stories.summary: The Health Ministry has proposed amending the 2019 New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules to classify antimicrobials as new drugs. The move aims to increase regulatory oversight and address antimicrobial resistance, which the Ministry identified as a priority following the G20 New Delhi Leaders' Declaration.

stories.title: Antimicrobials proposed for central regulatory oversight
stories.summary: The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has issued a draft notification to include antimicrobials in the definition of new drugs. The amendment seeks to strengthen oversight and combat antimicrobial resistance, following concerns regarding the current process for granting manufacturing licences.

stories.title: Bulk drug wholesale licensing framework proposed
stories.summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed a separate licensing framework for the wholesale of bulk drugs. The plan introduces dedicated application and licence forms to replace the current common licence, aiming for more focused regulatory oversight of the pharmaceutical supply chain.

stories.title: Government reserves more treatments for public hospitals
stories.summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed reserving 112 treatment packages for government hospitals under the Ayushman Bharat scheme, up from 23. The move could limit where beneficiaries can access cashless treatment, depending on the specific policies adopted by individual states.

stories.title: Health Ministry targets antimicrobial resistance
stories.summary: The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare is seeking to bring antimicrobials under a central regulatory framework. A draft notification dated November 6 invites public suggestions on the proposal, which aims to address concerns about how manufacturing licences for these products are currently issued.

stories.title: Antibiotics lose effectiveness against common infections
stories.summary: An ICMR report finds that antibiotics used for urinary, bloodstream and hospital-acquired infections are losing effectiveness. Laboratory tests show high resistance to drugs including cefotaxime and ciprofloxacin. The council warns of shrinking treatment options as antimicrobial resistance continues to grow across hospitals in India.

stories.title: ICMR identifies gaps in malaria reporting
stories.summary: Inadequate reporting from the private healthcare sector and discrepancies between estimated and official records are challenging India's malaria elimination efforts. Researchers also noted the potential circulation of rarely reported parasite species, which complicates the current understanding of the disease burden across the country.

stories.title: ICMR report highlights widespread antibiotic resistance
stories.summary: The 2025 ICMR report indicates that several antibiotics are showing low effectiveness against bacteria including E. coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae and Salmonella. The findings also flag resistance to powerful carbapenem drugs across participating hospitals, highlighting the scale of the challenge facing the national healthcare system.

stories.title: ICMR launches infectious disease surveillance network
stories.summary: The ICMR has launched a syndromic surveillance initiative to provide early warnings of disease outbreaks. The network will use real-time health data across 70 Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratories to provide immediate analysis and feedback for epidemiological investigations into potential public health threats.

stories.title: Health groups demand transparency on India TB data
stories.summary: Public health network Jan Swasthya Abhiyan India has petitioned authorities for systemic accountability regarding tuberculosis data. India accounts for roughly 25 percent of global infections and 23 percent of disease-related deaths. Advocates argue that clinical progress requires transparent epidemiology reporting alongside dependable supply chains.

stories.title: Health Ministry urged to explain Sabah’s RM1.06 million unpaid migrant medical bills - Daily Express Malaysia
Health ministry issues warning on GLP-1 eye risks
stories.summary: The Ministry of Health has issued an alert regarding a rare optic nerve disorder linked to GLP-1 medications and tirzepatide. The advisory follows a US FDA update concerning non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, a condition that can cause sudden and potentially permanent vision loss.

stories.title: Ministry investigates human rabies case in Kfar Ruth
stories.summary: The Health Ministry is investigating a human rabies case after a woman was diagnosed in critical condition. Officials believe the exposure source was a puppy found in August that died shortly after. The ministry has begun vaccinating individuals who may have had contact with the animal.

stories.title: Spain records 574 euthanasias in 2025
stories.summary: Spain's Ministry of Health reported 574 euthanasia procedures in 2025, a 35.7 percent increase from the previous year. Since the law took effect in 2021, 1,698 procedures have been completed. Nearly a third of applicants died while their requests were being processed.

stories.title: United States loses measles elimination status
stories.summary: The Pan American Health Organization has declared measles resurgent in the United States, ending a 26-year record of elimination. The virus has spread continuously for 12 months, marking the worst outbreak since 1991. The Americas were once the only measles-free region recognized by the WHO.

Measles resurgence marks public health backslide
stories.summary: International health officials confirmed the United States no longer meets the criteria for measles elimination. The finding follows a committee meeting of the Pan American Health Organization. The loss of status is widely viewed as a symbolic recognition of ongoing transmission and a decline in public health standing.

stories.title: Ebola outbreak in Congo continues to spread
stories.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo remains out of control six months after its declaration. Over 11,000 people have been infected and 5,500 have died. Resource shortages and distrust of outsiders continue to hamper containment efforts in the region.

stories.title: Ebola infections rising at record pace in DRC
stories.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is spreading faster than any previous recorded instance. Official data shows infections and deaths are rising at double the rate of past outbreaks. Despite aid, insecurity and poor coordination continue to complicate the response.

stories.title: Health Ministry : Number of wounded in Saudi aggression attack on capital Sana'a rises to 16 - وكالة سبأ
Palestinian woman killed in West Bank village
stories.summary: A 72-year-old Palestinian woman was shot dead in the village of al-Duyuk al-Tahta. The Palestinian health ministry reported the death following an incident involving Israeli settlers. Conflicting accounts describe either a settler attack or a car-ramming incident followed by gunfire.

stories.title: Bolivian doctors declare state of emergency
stories.summary: Bolivia's National Medical Council has declared a state of emergency, challenging decisions by the health minister regarding medical residency and social security codes. The guild has threatened nationwide protests and a formal demand for the minister's resignation if their concerns are not addressed.

stories.title: IntelliProve raises €2.7M to bring health monitoring from smartphones to humanoid robots - Tech.eu
August AI raises $12 million for US expansion
stories.summary: August AI has raised $12 million from Accel, Peak XV Partners, and Claypond Capital to expand its healthcare assistant in the US. The startup claims to have helped 10 million people understand their health through its AI companion. The funding follows a previous $3 million seed round.

stories.title: Ghent-based IntelliProve raises €2.7 million to monitor vital signs with a 30-second face scan using any camera - EU-Sta
Axena Health wins digital health award
stories.summary: Axena Health has been named a Best in Class winner in the Women's and Family Health category at the 2026 Digital Health and AI Awards. The company provides non-invasive treatments for pelvic health conditions. It notes that many women are told incontinence is a normal part of life.

stories.title: IntelliProve raises €2.7M to put its face-scan health check on robots - Dealroom
AccurKardia Named a Rising Star Winner at the 2026 Digital Health Hub to Digital Health & AI Awards at HLTH USA - Busine
Consint.ai and Pramana HealthTech partner in Asia-Pacific
stories.summary: Consint.ai and Pramana HealthTech have formed a partnership to create an AI-driven connected health ecosystem across the Asia-Pacific region. The collaboration aims to link payers, providers, pharmacies, and labs. The effort is described as advancing human health continuity through ecosystem orchestration and five interconnected transformation domains.

stories.title: CureMetrix named rising star at digital health awards
stories.summary: CureMetrix has been named a 2026 Rising Star winner at the Digital Health and AI Awards held at HLTH USA.

stories.title: Covenant Health earns digital health designations
stories.summary: Covenant Health has received Level 8 Acute and Level 9 Ambulatory designations in the 2026 CHIME Digital Health Most Wired survey. The recognition tracks the health system's digital infrastructure and technology adoption.

stories.title: Obtelecare receives two national health awards
stories.summary: Obtelecare has been named a winner in the Rising Star track of the Women's and Family Health category at the 2026 Digital Health and AI Awards. The company also placed as a runner-up for HealthTechNode's 2026 Women's HealthTech Advancement Award for its virtual maternal-fetal medicine services.

stories.title: DASI Simulations named to digital health list
stories.summary: CB Insights has named DASI Simulations to its 2026 Digital Health 50 list. The company uses AI-powered predictive modeling for structural heart care. An analyst noted that AI is beginning to change how healthcare organizations operate and how they deliver care.

stories.title: Eyonis Inc, a Median Technologies Company, Wins “Rising Star” Digital Health & AI Award for eyonis® LCS Lung Cancer Scre
Italian study links mental health to behavioral factors
stories.summary: A study tracking Italian public health metrics from 2016 to 2023 links psychological well-being to behavioral habits and environmental factors. Researchers used machine learning and regression models on ISTAT-BES data to identify how lifestyle patterns correlate with regional mental health disparities.

stories.title: Polish patients face mental health burden from rare disease
stories.summary: A study of patients with dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa in Poland reveals significant psychological distress alongside physical symptoms. The research highlights systemic barriers to care in Central and Eastern Europe, where patients report limited access to specialized multidisciplinary management and innovative therapies for the rare genetic disorder.

stories.title: Saudi study finds gender differences in mental health stigma
stories.summary: A survey of 586 residents in Jizan, Saudi Arabia, indicates that men hold slightly higher stigmatizing attitudes toward mental illness than women. The study used the Community Attitudes toward the Mentally Ill scale to measure public perceptions, finding a small statistical disparity between the two groups.

stories.title: UK study to track social media ban impact
stories.summary: The UK will launch a study involving 300,000 young people to examine the effects of a planned social media ban for under-16s. Ten research projects will monitor phone usage and alternative activities before the government restrictions begin in spring 2027.

stories.title: Deep brain stimulation study targets depression
stories.summary: Researchers from the Chinese Academy of Sciences and Shenzhen University have developed a noninvasive deep brain stimulation method. The approach aims to enhance reward learning and improve depressive symptoms in individuals with subclinical depression.

stories.title: Students increasingly turn to AI for mental health
stories.summary: The 2026 Cibyl Student Mental Health Study finds that 33 percent of students use AI tools for mental health support. While chatbot usage has risen, reliance on traditional human support routes including friends, family, and university medical teams has declined since 2021.

stories.title: LGBTQ+ youth turn to AI for mental health support
stories.summary: The Trevor Project reports that four in 10 queer young people have used AI chatbots for mental health support. The organization notes that these youth face higher rates of mental health struggles and barriers to care. Many are turning to algorithms to find the community they lack.

stories.title: Mental health crisis in children is real, say experts as cases soar fourfold - Medical Xpress
Weekly park visits linked to better mental health in children
stories.summary: A study of 4,219 British children published in the Journal of Epidemiology and Community Health found that those visiting parks weekly scored 16.5 percent better on mental health assessments. The research followed participants from birth to age 11. Nature remains a consistent variable in development.

stories.title: Oregon study reports outcomes from psilocybin therapy
stories.summary: A study of Oregon's state-regulated psilocybin program shows decreased symptoms of mental illness following supervised use of hallucinogenic mushrooms. Researchers describe the findings as a look at psilocybin in the real world. The state was the first to legalize the substance for therapeutic use.

stories.title: Wellcome funds study on UK social media ban
stories.summary: The Wellcome foundation is providing 9.3 million pounds to study the effects of the UK social media ban for under 16s. Ten teams will track over 300,000 young people to assess mental health outcomes. This is described as the largest scientific assessment of such restrictions worldwide.

stories.title: Study links junk food to cognitive and mental health issues
stories.summary: A review led by Flinders University associates high consumption of energy-dense, nutrient-poor foods and sugary drinks with poor mental health and academic performance in young people. Experts are calling for more community awareness regarding the impact of diet on cognitive development and the potential for future disorders.

research.title: A little-known protein could be a powerful weapon against Alzheimer’s
research.summary: Scientists have uncovered a powerful natural defense against Alzheimer’s disease that could open the door to new treatments. By boosting a protein called SORLA, researchers significantly reduced toxic tau tangles, protected connections between brain cells, and prevented some of the brain shrinkage associated with neurodegeneration in mice. research.title: A rare disease reveals a hidden flaw in the immune system
research.summary: Scientists have discovered that a rare, potentially life-threatening inflammatory disorder is driven by malfunctioning immune cells, overturning three decades of scientific understanding. The breakthrough points to a promising new treatment using existing medications, with one severely affected infant already showing substantial improvement.

research.title: MIT discovers that aging weakens the brain’s nighttime cleaning system
research.summary: MIT researchers have discovered that the brain’s natural waste-removal system becomes significantly less effective during sleep as people age. The decline is linked to weaker deep-sleep brain waves and changes in blood flow, potentially offering new clues about why aging increases the risk of Alzheimer's disease and dementia.

research.title: Tiny magnets deep inside the brain could transform Parkinson’s treatment
research.summary: Scientists have developed a new technique that uses magnetic nanoparticles to stimulate deep brain regions, dramatically improving Parkinson’s-like movement problems in mice without permanently implanted electrodes. The breakthrough could pave the way for less invasive treatments using injectable particles and wearable magnetic headbands.
